question: An events officer changed four things about her request at once and the result improved. She now wants to keep improving it over the coming weeks. What is the drawback of working this way?
options: A) She cannot tell which of the four changes helped, so she has learned nothing she can rely on next time.
B) The four changes together make the request considerably longer than the version she originally started from.
C) Changing four things at once takes more of her time than changing one thing and reviewing the result.
D) The improvement may not last, because results vary from one attempt to the next even with identical wording.
correct_answers: A) She cannot tell which of the four changes helped, so she has learned nothing she can rely on next time.
explanations: Correct. Bundled changes produce a result but no knowledge. Two of the four may have helped, one may have made no difference and one may have hurt, and she carries all four forward without knowing which is which.
A longer request is a side effect rather than the problem, and length is acceptable when every part of it is earning its place.
Changing several things at once is quicker in the moment, so effort is not what she loses by doing it.
Some variation between attempts is normal, but that is a reason to check a change more than once rather than an argument against improving the request.
